plugins.description: Codex-style window-swap compaction engine: deterministic pointer-template summaries with zero LLM calls, replacing the default LLM-summary compaction.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-compaction-codex

Codex 式换窗压缩引擎——彻底替换官方 dsh-compaction-basic 的「LLM 摘要式压缩」。

## 机制

- 继承官方 `BasicCompactionEngine`，只覆写官方承诺的唯一子类钩子 `summarize()`；
- 摘要改为**纯确定性指针模板（零 LLM 调用）**：归档声明 + 恢复通道指引（history_search / history_read / notes read）+ 最近 model 检查点笔记全文（读 `~/.dsh/context-budget/notes/<sid>.jsonl`，只读）+ 被归档区首尾消息截断锚点；
- SummaryResult 走官方契约的模板分支（无 `llmStreamCall` 字段，官方注释点名 "template, remote, or other summarizer"），转录中 `compaction/summary` 事件显示 `provider: template, model: codex-rollover`；
- shadow 事务、replay 定价、工具配对平衡、并发锁、阈值自动触发（0.8×窗口，router-standard 为 0.55）、context-overflow 恢复、/compact（compactNow）全部原样继承。

## 装配

- 源码：`~/.dsh/plugins-src/dsh-compaction-codex/`（本目录），构建：`bash scripts/build.sh`（链接 dsh-install 类型依赖 + tsc 编译 src → lib）；
- profile 链：`~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-compaction-codex` 软链 + `package.json` link 依赖（防 pnpm install 剪掉）；
- 预设：6 个用户预设（code / code-guarded / code-lean / dshagent / designharness / router-standard）compaction 组中 `compaction-basic` 条目已替换为 `compaction-codex`（2026-09-29，各文件留有 `.bak-20260929` 备份）；
- 生效范围：仅新会话（预设热扫描；运行中会话保持旧代装配）。

## 约束与边缘

- 官方 `summarizeCompaction` 要求摘要帧 token 数 < 被 shadow 内容 token 数；本模板上限约 5K 字符（约 1.5K tokens），对数千 tokens 以上的压缩区安全；极小压缩区会按官方逻辑抛错并留在日志（不会静默）；
- notes 文件缺失/损坏时自动降级（省略检查点段），不阻塞压缩事务；
- 回滚：预设 yml 中把 name 改回 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic`（或恢复 .bak）即回官方 LLM 摘要，热生效（新会话）。

## 决策记录

- 2026-09-29 用户拍板：方案 A（子类替换）+ 纯 Codex 式（永不 LLM 摘要，无混合开关）；
- 否决方案 B（从零实现抽象 CompactionEngine：需重写 shadow 持久化/锁/配对平衡，收益零风险高）与方案 C（拆压缩组：长会话必撞上下文硬上限）。

plugins.description: 余额水桶：水位就是你的 DeepSeek API 余额，出水口流出的是正在花的钱。A bucket that drains while your DeepSeek API balance is being spent (DeepSeek Harness plugin).
plugins.readme_text:
# Balance Bucket · 余额水桶

**A little bucket that drains while your DeepSeek API balance is being spent.**

![Six bucket states: full, pouring, low, refilled, unreadable, and dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/youchai2016/dsh-plugin-token-bucket/v0.1.1/docs/images/bucket-states.png)

一只挂在窗口角落的小水桶。**水是你的余额，漏出去的是正在花的钱。**

Version 0.1.1.

## What it does

- **The water level is your real balance.** It reads `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` with the same `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` that DSH chats with, so the bucket shows the money you actually have.
- **The water is two layers, because the money is.** Granted balance (赠送) floats on top of topped-up balance (充值). DeepSeek deducts the granted wallet first, so you watch the pale layer empty before the deep one moves.
- **The tap opens while money moves.** The stream and its droplets are proportional to the burn rate over the last three minutes — the tool for watching a `vibe coding` session eat your credit.
- **The bucket is as tall as the highest balance it has ever seen.** It starts full, and a top-up makes it taller rather than overflowing.
- **A failed read never lies.** If the balance cannot be read, the water stays where it was, the tap shuts, and the outline turns amber. It never empties the bucket to show an error.

Move it, resize it, tuck it away — right-click for settings, drag to reposition, arrow keys to nudge.

## Reading the bucket

| Look | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Pale layer on top | Granted balance (spent first) |
| Deep layer below | Topped-up balance |
| Blue water | Above 30% of the highest balance seen |
| Amber water | Between 10% and 30% |
| Red water, gentle wobble | Below 10% |
| Amber outline, no stream | The last read failed; the level is the last known one |
| Grey water, `—` | No API key configured, or the key was rejected |

Hover the bucket for the numbers, or open the settings panel for balance, granted/topped-up split, spent since start, added since start, burn rate, bucket size and the age of the last reading.

## Install

Package page: [dsh-plugin-token-bucket on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-token-bucket).

```text
dsh-plugin-token-bucket
```

Or pin this release:

```text
github:youchai2016/dsh-plugin-token-bucket#v0.1.0
```

The plugin needs the credential DSH already manages for chat. If the Models page has a working DeepSeek API key, the bucket works; if not, it says so instead of guessing.

## Privacy and runtime boundaries

- The API key is resolved through DSH's credential service on every poll and is **never** stored, logged, echoed in an error, or sent to the client half. The browser half never talks to the balance service itself.
- **One** outbound request exists: a read-only `GET` on the documented balance endpoint. No model calls, no telemetry, no listening port, no third-party service.
- Nothing about your conversations is read. This plugin subscribes to **no** session events, so it cannot see prompts, replies or tool output.
- Preferences and history live in the browser's local storage. The plugin never writes your DSH profile.

## Honest limits

- The burn rate is **estimated from balance deltas**, not from token counts: the balance moves in whole cents (¥0.01), so the reading is a rolling three-minute average rather than a per-request figure. It is deliberately not a billing statement.
- Polling is adaptive: every 5 seconds for two minutes after money moves, then 20 seconds, then once a minute while nothing happens. Change calls from other devices or tools are also visible, because they move the same balance.
- Prices, bonuses and the split between granted and topped-up balance are whatever the API reports. The bucket does not compute costs from a price list.
- Balances are read for one currency, preferring CNY.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
npm test
```

`preview/index.html` is a single offline file: open it in a browser, no server and no network needed. Its buttons fabricate balance samples, so every state can be inspected without an API key.

The Host half is bundled to `lib/index.js`, the strict browser/Host contract to `lib/remote.js`, and the browser half to `lib/client.js` by `pnpm run build`. Prebuilt files are committed so a Git install needs no build step.

## License

Code is [MIT](LICENSE). No third-party artwork is bundled: the bucket is drawn with CSS and one inline SVG.

plugins.description: A desktop pet that shows what your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness) are doing — and lets you answer their permission prompts
plugins.readme_text:
# agent-pet

A floating desktop pet for coding agents. One character per active agent (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, or anything that can run a shell command); her mood follows the agent, and when an agent asks for permission the pet shows the prompt in a bubble you can answer without switching windows.

![agent-pet showing a permission bubble](docs/screenshot.png)

Pets appear only while a session is working, waiting for you, or just finished. Everything is local: agents append JSON lines to a file and the overlay tails it. Nothing is sent over the network and there are no accounts; the optional DSH plugin opens a loopback-only port (127.0.0.1) for the overlay's open-session commands.

## Requirements

- macOS 14 or later
- Swift 6 toolchain (Xcode or the Command Line Tools)
- Python 3 (ships with macOS; used by the installer)

ChatGPT (the chat app) has no local plugin API, so there is no integration with it. Codex running inside ChatGPT.app is covered by the Codex plugin below.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rpegorov/agent-pet.git
cd agent-pet
scripts/install.sh                  # build, install to ~/.local/agent-pet, hook up Claude Code and Codex
scripts/install.sh --launch-agent   # also start the overlay at login
```

`install.sh` also accepts `--no-claude-hooks` and `--no-codex-hooks` (use these with the plugins below), and `--uninstall`.

## Connect your agents

Use **either** the plugin **or** the `install.sh` hooks for a given agent, not both. Both together would deliver every event twice and ask every permission twice; the emitter does not de-duplicate because it cannot tell which hook fired first. Plugins carry only the hook wiring, so run `scripts/install.sh --no-claude-hooks --no-codex-hooks` once for the binary and the overlay.

**Claude Code.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json`. Or, as a plugin:

```
/plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
/plugin install agent-pet@agent-pet
```

**Codex.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.codex/hooks.json` and trusts them in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Or, as a plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
codex plugin add codex-agent-pet@agent-pet
```

Codex does not trust the plugin's hooks on a command-line install, so they stay silent until you approve them (see Troubleshooting). The `install.sh` route has no such step.

**DeepSeek Harness (DSH).** `plugins/dsh-agent-pet` is a standalone DSH plugin. In your profile's `package.json` add a dependency `"dsh-agent-pet": "link:/path/to/agent-pet/plugins/dsh-agent-pet"` and add `"dsh-agent-pet"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, install, and restart DSH. It reports session state and lets the overlay open a session or start a chat in the Harness UI.

**Anything else** (scripts, task runners, other agents):

```sh
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --label "refactor" --mood working
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --mood complete
```

## Event protocol

`agent-pet-emit` appends one line per event to `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` (override with `AGENT_PET_LOG`); the overlay tails the file. The file is rotated to `events.jsonl.1` above 512 KiB.

```json
{"v":1,"agent":"claude","session":"5e9d","mood":"working","label":"Bash","ts":1792276251.42}
```

`mood` is `idle`, `working`, `attention`, `complete` or `ended` (removes the session). `label` is at most 40 characters. Optional fields, omitted when unknown: `cwd`, `app` (bundle id of the hosting app), `tty`, `detail` (permission summary, at most 200 characters), `permission` (id of a pending request).

Decay: working with no event for 120 s is hidden, complete is hidden after 10 s, attention after 10 min, a session silent for 30 min is dropped. An agent's pet shows the highest-priority mood of its live sessions: attention, working, complete.

## Permission bubble

With the overlay running, `agent-pet-emit permit` (the PermissionRequest hook) shows the pending tool call in a bubble with **Deny**, **In agent** and **Allow**, and a countdown.

- The bubble shows the whole tool input (pretty-printed JSON, capped at 8 KiB). If the input is capped or unreadable, Allow is withheld.
- **In agent** hands the prompt back to the agent's own dialog. If nobody answers before the countdown ends (at most 40 s, `AGENT_PET_PERMIT_WAIT` seconds, default 30), or the overlay stops running, the native dialog appears as usual. The pet never auto-allows.
- Tools that ask you something (`AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`) are never turned into a bubble.
- Requests live in `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` (owner-only) and are removed when answered, expired or when the hook is killed.
- The overlay's own texts (Deny, In agent, Allow, status labels) are English and not localised; labels that come from agents (tool names, session titles) appear as sent.
- To turn the bubble off, quit the overlay (the hook then stays silent), or change the `PermissionRequest` command from `permit` to `hook` in the agent's hook config.

## Privacy

agent-pet keeps everything on your Mac and sends nothing over the network.

- **What is written.** `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` holds one line per hook event: agent name, session id, mood, a short label (tool name, session title or notification text), the working directory, the hosting app's bundle id, the terminal tty and, for permission requests, a summary of the tool call (at most 200 characters). Prompts, tool output and file contents are not recorded.
- **Permission requests.** While a request is pending, `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` holds its full tool input (at most 8 KiB). The file is deleted when the request is answered, expires or the hook is killed; leftovers older than 2 minutes are cleaned up.
- **Access.** The directory is owner-only (0700) and the log is 0600. The log is rotated at 512 KiB, keeping one previous file.
- **What is read.** The overlay reads the event log, and, to open a Claude Desktop session, the session index in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions` (read only). Selecting a Terminal or iTerm2 tab uses AppleScript and asks macOS for Automation permission once.
- **System log.** Clicks and jumps are logged under the subsystem `agent-pet` with agent, session id, app and the opened URL; no tool input or paths.
- **Network.** None outbound. The DSH plugin listens on a loopback-only port and accepts commands only from local processes and the Harness web UI; the overlay talks to it over `127.0.0.1`.

Delete `~/.agent-pet` to remove all recorded data.

## Uninstall

```sh
scripts/install.sh --uninstall
```

Removes the binaries, hooks, trust entries and LaunchAgent. A no-op `agent-pet-emit` stub stays behind so sessions that are still open do not report a missing command; restart them and delete the stub. Plugins are removed with `/plugin uninstall`, `codex plugin remove` or by editing the DSH profile.

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing appears.** Is the overlay running (`pgrep -x AgentPet`)? Does `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` grow when an agent works? If not, the hooks are not installed or the agent was started before they were; restart the agent.
- **Codex plugin hooks do nothing.** Codex 0.163 does not trust hooks from a plugin installed with `codex plugin add`; they ran only with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. Approve them in Codex (`/hooks`) or use `scripts/install.sh`, which writes the trust entries itself. Re-run `install.sh` after changing a hook command: the trust is tied to its text.
- **DSH changes are not picked up.** DSH caches plugin ES modules; restart it after installing or editing a plugin.
- **DSH commands are refused.** The plugin's bridge answers only the Harness web UI origin (`http://127.0.0.1:50306`) and local processes; a UI served from another origin cannot read its queue.

## License

MIT. The sprite art in `Sources/AgentPet/Resources` is included under the same license.

plugins.description: Live per-session cost badge for DeepSeek Harness (top-right), with peak/off-peak (time-of-day) pricing.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-cost-meter

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-2ea44f)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that puts a **live cost badge in the conversation header (top-right)** and prices every request with **peak / off-peak (time-of-day) tiers**.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Session title                                [¥0.0042]      │   ← badge here
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  … conversation …                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Features

- **Live** — the badge updates as the host reports provider usage; no polling, no timers.
- **Historically correct** — each request is priced by its **own wall-clock timestamp**, so a session that spans peak and off-peak stays accurate even if the page sits open overnight.
- **Weekday-aware peak tiers** — DeepSeek bills peak only **Monday–Friday**; weekends are off-peak all day. The schedule is configurable (windows, weekdays, multiplier, time zone).
- **Silent price sync** — a bundled price catalog plus an out-of-band remote catalog refreshed on an interval. Push a new `catalog/prices.json` and every installed copy picks it up **without a plugin release**; a failed refresh keeps the last good rates.
- **Explicit peak/off-peak rates** — models may carry an explicit discounted pair (`cacheMiss` + `cacheMissOffPeak`), not just a multiplier.
- **Route-aware matching** — `provider/model`, `provider/*`, `*`-model wildcards, and case/space/punctuation-insensitive model ids.
- **Never fakes a number** — an unpriced route renders `未配置` (`unpriced`) instead of a made-up fallback rate.

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-cost-meter
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` activates it as a profile layer automatically — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` row is required.

### From a local checkout

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:E:/path/to/dsh-plugin-cost-meter"
```

`link:` keeps the checkout live, so edits apply after a `dsh web` restart without reinstalling.

Restart the server afterwards:

```cmd
dsh web
```

## Configure

The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin row with defaults. Override it by adding a `cost-meter` row with the same `id` in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: cost-meter
      name: dsh-plugin-cost-meter
      config:
        currency: CNY                 # display currency; empty = catalog currency
        fx:
          cnyPerUsd: 7.1              # used when the catalog is USD and you display CNY
        catalogUrl: ""                # "" = this package's own catalog (derived from repository)
        refreshMinutes: 360           # silent refresh interval; 0 disables it
        pricingTimeoutMs: 4000
        pricingUrl: ""                # optional legacy { models, default } document
        models:                       # manual overrides (highest priority, display currency)
          deepseek-official/deepseek-flash:
            inputPerM: 1.06           # off-peak base
            cacheReadPerM: 0.021
            cacheWritePerM: 1.06
            outputPerM: 4.26
        default:                      # optional fallback; omit to report unknown routes as unpriced
          inputPerM: 1
          outputPerM: 4
        peak:
          enabled: true
          multiplier: 2               # used only when a rate has no explicit off-peak value
          timezoneOffsetMinutes: 480  # UTC+8
          days: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]       # ISO weekdays; weekends are off-peak
          windows: [[9, 12], [14, 18]]
```

Two rate styles are accepted everywhere:

- **Catalog style** (peak base + optional off-peak): `cacheMiss`, `cacheHit`, `cacheWrite`, `output`, and `cacheMissOffPeak`, `cacheHitOffPeak`, `cacheWriteOffPeak`, `outputOffPeak`.
- **Legacy style** (off-peak base): `inputPerM`, `cacheReadPerM`, `cacheWritePerM`, `outputPerM` (with optional `*Peak` fields).

## Automatic price updates

Prices resolve in this order (highest wins):

1. `config.models` / `config.default`
2. `config.pricingUrl` (legacy document)
3. the **remote catalog** at `config.catalogUrl` — default: this package's own `catalog/prices.json` on GitHub, derived from `package.json.repository`
4. the **bundled** `catalog/prices.json` (offline fallback)

A timer re-reads the remote catalog and `pricingUrl` every `refreshMinutes` (default 6 hours) and swaps the live table in place:

- a failed refresh **keeps the last successful data**;
- a source that never loaded does not clear anything;
- **historical amounts are frozen**: a sample is priced when it is folded and the amount is stored, so a price change applies only to samples folded after it — a past session's total is never rewritten;
- the frozen amounts ride the persisted projection cache, so they survive restarts; only a cold replay without a checkpoint prices the log at the then-current table.

This makes the catalog the single place to maintain rates: **edit and push `catalog/prices.json`, and installed copies update themselves** — no new plugin release. Forks get their own update channel automatically because the default URL is derived from `package.json.repository`.

To point at a private mirror or a local file, set `catalogUrl` (`https://…`, a path, or `file:///…`). Set it to `""` to disable remote syncing.

## Peak / off-peak

- Tiering uses the **request's own `event.time`**, never "now".
- Peak applies only on the configured weekdays (`days`, default Monday–Friday); weekends are off-peak all day.
- The schedule comes from the catalog's `peakSchedule` (time zone, days, windows, off-peak ratio) and can be overridden field by field in `config.peak`.
- `peak.enabled: false` bills one flat rate; `peak.timezoneOffsetMinutes` shifts the wall clock for the window check.

The hover tooltip shows the current tier, the multiplier, the route, and the token breakdown.

## Pricing model

```
cost = Σ_routes [ cost_off(route) + cost_peak(route) ]

cost_tier(route) = (uncachedInput × miss
                  + cacheRead     × hit
                  + cacheWrite    × write
                  + output        × out) / 1_000_000
```

Totals are accumulated per `{ provider, model }` route and per tier, so switching models mid-session keeps each route on its own price. A repeated usage sample for the same `(turn, step)` replaces the earlier one instead of double-counting.

## Compatibility

| Surface | DSH ≤ 0.1.0-rc.6 | DSH ≥ 0.1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Projection contract | `schema` + `view` | `stateSchema` + `wire: { viewSchema, view }` |
| Client deps | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` |
| Compatibility gate | — | `engines.dsh` / `peerDependencies` must satisfy the running version |

The badge uses the additive `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot; `…header.corner` is a `single` slot already occupied by a shipped plugin.

## Development

```cmd
npm install
npm test
```

`test/contract.test.mjs` covers the projection contract, weekday peak, catalog parsing, explicit dual rates, currency conversion, normalization/wildcards, unpriced routes, and manual overrides. It runs offline (`catalogUrl: ""`).

## Notes

- Costs are **estimates**: they depend on the provider-reported `usage` and on the price table.
- The badge is **per session**; it does not aggregate sub-sessions or the whole account.
- The bundled catalog is a dated snapshot — verify it against the [official pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing) and update `catalog/prices.json` when rates change.
- The plugin is a Web surface plugin; compositions without `sessionProjections` (e.g. headless) skip registration.

## Li

plugins.description: DSH community plugin: ask any set of models to draw a pelican riding a bicycle on a schedule, then lay every drawing out on a read-only board. No scoring — the pictures are the result. Pausable, with a settable interval.
plugins.readme_text:
# @mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

A DeepSeek Harness **community plugin** that runs a long-term
**model-quality probe** (降智监测) on a schedule, across **any number of
models**:

- **Pick your models** — the gear in the panel's top-right corner lists every model the
  configured providers report (live `/models` discovery, merged with the models
  in your DSH profile) and probes a multi-selected set, each model through its
  own provider and API key.
- **Scheduled drawing** — every 30 minutes (configurable) each selected model is
  asked to draw an **animated** *pelican riding a bicycle*: a single-file HTML
  page with an inline SVG whose motion is SVG declarative animation (`<animate>`
  / `<animateTransform>`).
- **No skills, no tools** — each run is a bare `chat/completions` request with
  no tool definitions and no agent loop, so the result measures the model
  alone, never your local skills.
- **Everything flat, nothing to click** — the main board is read-only: one band
  per model, its status and figures on the left (when its newest drawing landed,
  runs, average duration, how many came back without a drawing, and the failure
  reason) and every drawing it ever made on the right, all laid out at once —
  nothing collapsed, filtered, or hidden behind a click.
- **Run state in the header** — while probing: “n/m done”, which models are in
  flight, how long the slowest has waited (m:ss) and the timeout cap (m:ss), so a
  slow model and a stuck one are told apart at a glance.
- **One gear button** — the panel's own top-right corner opens a settings sheet:
  pick models, pause or retune the schedule, stop the pass, see one drawing
  bigger. The board below stays pure viewing, so nothing has to be clicked to be
  read. To probe **one** model, press 「单独检测」 on its band: one request for
  that model — and several bands can be probing at the same time.
- **Stop it, retune it** — that same sheet can **pause / resume automatic
  probing**, change the **interval** (1–1440 minutes), and **stop the pass that is
  running right now**: requests in flight are aborted, models that had not started
  are skipped without a request being sent. Pausing is written to
  `settings.json` immediately and survives a restart, so a plugin you only probe
  by hand never costs a token on its own.
- **Bounded history** — keeps the newest N drawings **per model** (10 by
  default); the cap never gets divided between the models you are probing, and
  two providers serving the same model id keep separate histories. Same prompt,
  same model, over days: degradation shows up as worse structure, refusals
  (saved and badged 「未检出 SVG」), or latency growth.

## Install

From this GitHub repository (recommended):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch.git
```

Or from a local path or tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-pelican-watch
```

Note: `link:`-installed plugins are not watched by HMR, so editing
`lib/index.js` or `lib/client.js` requires an app restart to take effect.

## Choosing models

The gear in the panel's top-right corner opens the settings sheet, which lists
**every provider route registered in DSH** — the signed-in 「DeepSeek 账号」
account, the official API-key route, and any third-party provider you configured
— grouped by the display name DSH uses, each with the models it advertises. Tick
any number of models and **Save models**: from the next cycle on each selected
model draws its own picture and gets its own band on the board.

**The board shows exactly the selected models**, in the order they were saved —
a band never jumps around. Unticking a model and saving **deletes its drawings**:
anything the board cannot show is only invisible dead weight on disk, and these
probe drawings are meant to be re-drawn anyway. The save toast says how many went.

A model id is not unique: the signed-in account and a third-party provider can
both serve `deepseek-flash`. A band is therefore a **provider + model** pair, and
it carries the provider's display name next to the model name — two providers
never share one band, nor one another's drawings.

The plugin never touches key material: calls go through DSH's model service
(`ctx.llm`), which resolves the credential itself. That is why the
account-backed provider (no API key at all, just a signed-in account) can be
probed here, and why any provider that works in DSH works here. A provider that
cannot list its models (not signed in, expired key) still appears, with the
reason attached.

That selection lives in `dir/settings.json` and is what the scheduler uses;
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the first run. The same file holds
two knobs that decide what you spend, both changeable from the panel's gear
without touching any config file:

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autoEnabled` | `true` | Off disarms the timer at once (`nextRunAt` goes empty); only the manual “probe now” then spends anything, and the choice survives a restart. |
| `intervalMinutes` | follows `config.intervalMinutes` (30) | Changing it in the panel re-arms the countdown immediately — no restart. |
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the very first run. At most 12
models are probed per cycle — `concurrency` of them at the same time (3 by
default), one drawing each.

## Speed and timeouts

- **Models run in parallel** (3 at a time by default), so one slow model no
  longer delays the others: every drawing is written to disk the moment it
  arrives and shows up in the panel within seconds.
- **Each request has its own timeout** (`timeoutSeconds`, default 600). A model
  that exceeds it is reported as `超过 N 秒没有返回` on its own band instead of
  hanging the whole pass. Reasoning models can genuinely be slow — measured
  against one provider: `qwen3.7-max` ~52s, `deepseek-flash` ~121s (15k of those
  completion tokens were reasoning), while `glm-5.3-flash` sometimes exceeded
  4 minutes.
- **A timeout or HTTP error is not a drawing**: nothing is saved and it does not
  count as a drawing, because that is an infrastructure fact rather than model
  behaviour. A model that *answers* without an SVG (a refusal) is saved and
  marked `没出图` — that is the signal worth looking at.
- `maxTokens` is not sent by default: reasoning models spend tens of thousands of
  completion tokens before they draw, and a tight ceiling would truncate the SVG
  instead of speeding anything up.
- **A truncated drawing is reported as such**: when the answer stops at the
  output ceiling (an `<svg>` without its closing tag), the band says
  「回答被截断（已输出 N tokens）：SVG 没有画完，多半是达到模型的输出上限」 instead of the
  vague 「未检出 SVG」, and the half-drawn page is not kept as history. Raise
  `maxTokens` in the config to give a verbose model more room.

## Configuration

Defaults match the usual profile setup; override any of them on a
`pelican-watch` row in your profile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: pelican-watch
  config:
    # initial selection (the panel's picker wins once used)
    provider: deepseek-account           # a DSH provider route; account by default
    model: deepseek-flash                # model id
    # targets:                           # optional: seed several models at once
    #   - { provider: deepseek-account, model: deepseek-flash }
    #   - { provider: taotoken, model: glm-5.3-flash }
    intervalMinutes: 30                  # drawing cadence
    maxImages: 10                        # drawings kept per model (1–100; ≈5h at 30min)
    timeoutSeconds: 600                  # per-request ceiling (5–3600); lower it if a model hangs
    concurrency: 3                       # how many models are probed at once
    # maxTokens: 8192                    # optional; unset by default (see below)
    dir: ~/.dsh/pelican-watch            # where drawings are saved
    runOnStart: true                     # draw once ~8s after boot
    # temperature: 0.7                   # optional; omitted by default
    # prompt: …                          # only if you must change the benchmark
```

The benchmark prompt is delibe

plugins.description: Second-opinion review for DeepSeek Harness sessions: a restricted child session re-reads the Executor's work with read-only tools and delivers severity-ranked advice.
plugins.readme_text:
# @wweir/dsh-advisor

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

An automatic second opinion for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

On a configurable per-round rhythm, a **restricted sub-agent** re-reads the
Executor's recent work with read-only tools. Concrete defects are recorded
and delivered to the Executor's inbox; when there is nothing to point
at, the reviewer stays silent — silence is the normal outcome, not a failure.

The plugin never runs its own model loop: the review is a real child session,
so the host's turn/step machine, tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation and
persistence apply to it unchanged.

## What it does for you

- **Catches hallucinations.** The reviewer reads the actual files (read-only):
  changes claimed but not made, APIs that do not exist, values never written.
  The note points at the mismatch while the work is fresh; delivery is
  advisory, interrupting only as configured.
- **Keeps sessions on track.** At most one review every N completed rounds
  (default 3), never concurrently — rounds arriving mid-review coalesce into a
  single catch-up. Drift is reported inside the running turn; idle sessions
  can be woken by severe findings (budgeted, severity-gated). Silence is
  reported as a result, not an error.
- **Bounded cost.** The reviewer's context is a compiled projection capped at
  32K tokens by default (≈ **25% of a 128K window**), never a copy of the
  Executor's. The projection marks where the work since the last completed
  review begins, and the prompt asks the reviewer to judge that part first —
  concluding within three steps and batching independent reads. The boundary
  line carries a nonce minted per review, so a phrase quoted inside the
  evidence cannot pose as it. A stable instruction prefix lets the provider's
  context cache
  hit across reviews (cache-read tokens are shown in the tab and billed at
  cache rates). Output is a single advice of at most 2K characters.

## Why

Most advisor plugins hand the transcript to one extra LLM call and inject
whatever comes back. This plugin makes the reviewer a **real child session with
its own read-only tools**, which buys four concrete things:

- **It verifies instead of guessing.** The reviewer opens the files the
  Executor actually touched, so a note points at a defect it looked at — not
  a pattern inferred from a transcript summary, which is all a
  transcript-only reviewer can ever offer.
- **The host's rules apply to the review itself.** Turn/step accounting, the
  tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation, persistence, and a real audit
  trail: the review is a session you can inspect, and its cost is reported
  usage, not an estimate.
- **Isolation is enforced, not promised.** One reviewer claim per process, a
  read-only tool surface, a protected-path guard deliberately stricter than
  the upstream advisor (workspace-root private keys and `.envrc` included),
  and no shared context with the Executor.
- **Delivery is accounted.** A note counts as delivered only when the host
  proves it was processed (a follow-up turn's model reply); an unconfirmed
  note is requeued, never silently dropped. Repetition is suppressed by
  finding identity plus similarity, with hash-based mutes.

## Install

The package is a Cordis plugin (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`) and is
published on npm with a provenance attestation, so it installs like any other
profile bundle:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @wweir/dsh-advisor
```

A development checkout can be linked instead (`dsh plugin … add /path/to/checkout`);
its deploy path is described in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

Then give it a model route. It is **disabled until a model is configured**, and
it never falls back to the Executor's model:

```yaml
- id: advisor
  name: '@wweir/dsh-advisor'
  config:
    enabled: true
    model:
      provider: opencode-go
      model: glm-5.3-flash
      reasoningEffort: low
    instructions: ''            # extra review instructions, appended to the prompt
    review:
      everyTurns: 3             # minimum completed rounds between two reviews
      timeoutMs: 180000         # wall-clock bound for one review
      maxContextTokens: 32000   # material sent to the reviewer
      maxAdviceChars: 2000      # one advice body
      maxPending: 32            # queued, not-yet-delivered notes
    delivery:
      activeIdleSeverities: [concern, blocker]   # severities allowed to wake an idle Executor
    security:
      additionalProtectedPaths: []      # extra paths the reviewer may never read
```

A patch entry is **replaced, not merged**, per row id: an overlay that sets
only the extra instructions drops the model route, and the row stops loading —
loudly, with a validation error.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- **Trigger** — one review *round*: the Executor's final answer, or, for a
  turn that closes without one, the end of a top-level turn that completes,
  hits its token limit, or errors. Rounds are the unit because a reader can
  keep steering into a running turn: that turn never ends, and a turn-based
  trigger would never fire even though every reply was a completed round.
  Sub-agent sessions (including the review children) are never reviewed.
  Turns this plugin opened itself are never reviewed either.
- **Delivery** — while the Executor is running the note is handed into the
  next step boundary; while it is idle the note may open an exclusive turn,
  but only for a severity allowed to wake an idle session (by default
  concern and blocker), at most 5 times per session; anything else waits for
  a later flush. A note delivered into a running turn is recorded as
  delivered once the host accepts it. A note that opened an exclusive turn is
  recorded **only after that turn emits a model reply**: the hand-off alone
  does not prove the note was read, so a turn that closes (restart,
  interrupt, empty turn) without a reply puts the note back in the queue,
  marked as already attempted — it will not open a second follow-up turn, but
  the next running turn can still receive it. The confirmation is persisted
  immediately, and an unconfirmed claim found in the sidecar on load is
  requeued the same way. A delivered finding is suppressed by identity, so a
  reworded repeat is not re-delivered.
- **Failure pause** — three consecutive *real* failures (model error, timeout,
  bad tool surface) pause automatic review. Cancellations are counted separately:
  they are recorded but never pause. A pause holds for the life of the loaded
  plugin; **a plugin reload (a profile-row change or a process restart) clears
  the tripwire** and re-arms review. Saving the page's configuration form is not
  a reload and leaves a paused advisor paused.
- **State** — one JSON sidecar per Executor session under
  `$DSH_HOME/advisor/` (default `~/.dsh/advisor/`). It holds the review
  cursor, the dedupe table, the pending queue, the mute list, and the failure
  accounting as diagnostics. A file that does not parse is never overwritten
  and is reported in the host log.
- **Mutes** — add `{ "hash": "<64-hex hash of the finding>", "label": "..." }`
  to the sidecar's `mutes` list. Identity is the full hash; there is no
  prefix matching.
- **Page surface** — the web client shows an **Advisor** tab beside
  Chat/Trajectory/Host. It reads the same state as `/advisor status` over the
  same authenticated channel as the GUI itself (browser session cookie and
  Host/Origin fence apply) and
  refreshes every few seconds, so a paused advisor and the reason for the last
  silence are visible without typing a command. Presentation is one injected
  stylesheet over DSH theme tokens, so light/dark, focus, hover and touch sizing
  follow the host; sections are headings inside labelled regions, and the polled
  state is mirrored in a polite live region for screen readers. Its queue block
  is the delivery surface, ordered by what the reader acts on: the live figures
  first (pending notes with the reason the head note is **held** — executor
  running, severity not allowed to wake an idle session, follow-up budget spent,
  a previous attempt went unprocessed, a newer instruction arrived — notes
  **awaiting confirmat

plugins.description: Offline HAR diagnostics with minimal evidence for DeepSeek Harness
plugins.readme_text:
# HAR Triage

Offline network evidence for DeepSeek Harness. Find failed and slow browser requests without handing the agent your URLs, cookies or response bodies.

浏览器网络排障插件：读取本地 HAR，生成可回查原始请求索引的离线诊断报告。默认不把网址、请求头、Cookie、参数值或正文带进报告和 AI 工具结果。

![Synthetic HAR diagnosis: signals, source indexes and timing evidence](docs/report-demo.jpg)

The screenshot uses the bundled synthetic scenario, not real browser traffic.

## What it does

- Reads an existing HAR 1.2 capture; never records traffic, sends requests, or changes the capture.
- Groups requests into endpoint aliases, highlights HTTP 4xx/5xx, unavailable responses, slow requests and long waiting phases.
- Produces a self-contained HTML report: signals → request row → measured timing phases. Filters, pagination and source locators work offline.
- Returns at most 20 evidence entries to the agent, with a count of omitted evidence. The full numeric projection stays in the local JSON/HTML files.

Request #43 corresponds to `log.entries[42]` in your original HAR. Endpoint aliases deliberately do not reveal names. Keep the original capture private and use its index to look up the actual request locally.

## Install in Harness

Node 22.19+ is required. Install the prebuilt bundle into your chosen profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE add https://github.com/po-et/dsh-har-triage/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-har-triage-0.1.0.tgz
dsh --profile YOUR_PROFILE --dump-config
```

The configuration should contain the `har-triage` row. Start that profile, put your HAR inside its session workspace, and ask:

> Inspect capture.har with har_triage. Save reports in a new har-review directory. Explain the measured evidence and cite the original HAR entry indexes. Do not guess root causes.

Tool arguments:

```json
{"input":"capture.har","outputDir":"har-review","slowMs":2000}
```

The tool uses Harness filesystem and sandbox services. It requires write permission to create the reports and refuses input/output paths outside the session workspace. Existing report files are never overwritten. Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE remove dsh-har-triage`.

## Try without Harness

The CLI and analysis/report modules use Node built-ins only. From a source checkout:

```sh
node src/cli.js capture.har --out new-report-directory --slow-ms 2000
```

Open `new-report-directory/report.html`. The output directory must not exist. The original capture is unchanged.

For a reproducible synthetic example:

```sh
npm run demo
```

This creates a new directory under `artifacts/` with a deliberately synthetic capture and its report. It is not evidence of real browser traffic or real users.

## Evidence, not root-cause claims

`503` means the capture records a server-error response. `status: 0` means it did not record a valid HTTP response. Neither identifies a failing service, proves CORS, or proves an expired token. A high wait/TTFB share is an observation, not proof that the backend or database is slow.

Start offsets include submillisecond differences and are expressed in relative milliseconds. Absolute source timestamps are never included in the report.

Unknown phase timings and byte sizes remain `-1`, displayed as “Unknown.” TLS is part of the HAR connection timing and is not added a second time. Contradictory phase durations are flagged; the report hides misleading proportions.

Ollama's [`application/x-ndjson` streaming responses](https://docs.ollama.com/api/streaming) are classified as JSON. This is a MIME-based content category, not validation of the response body; model output remains excluded from reports.

## What is retained and removed

Retained: source entry index, sequential endpoint alias, controlled method/status/content classes, relative offsets, numeric durations/sizes, and fixed diagnostic codes. Aliases group the same method/origin/path within one capture; query strings and fragments do not affect grouping.

HTTP method identity is case-sensitive: `GET` and `get` receive separate aliases. Only the allowlisted uppercase methods receive named display values; all other method tokens appear as `OTHER`. Private method tokens are used only for grouping and are not included in reports, tool evidence or report ID hashes.

Removed: complete URLs including origins and paths, query values, headers, cookies, request/response bodies, page titles, initiator data, IP addresses, absolute timestamps, extension fields, raw error text, and the original file digest. The report ID hashes only the retained projection. Arbitrary source strings are not copied to reports or tool evidence.

This is a minimal diagnostic projection, **not** a scrubbed HAR, an anonymization guarantee, or a replacement for reviewing an artifact before sharing it. Status patterns, sizes, timing, request counts and grouping can still identify an application. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Limits

- HAR JSON only: version `1.2`, UTF-8, at most 16 MiB and 10,000 entries. Invalid supported entries fail with fixed errors rather than silently truncating the evidence.
- HTTP and HTTPS requests are analyzed. Other protocols are excluded and counted. Missing timing/size values are retained as unknown; a valid request URL, start timestamp, duration, status and response content object are required.
- Synchronous bounded analysis: cancellation is checked before parsing and between entries, not an interruptible worker. The slow threshold defaults to 2,000 ms and is configurable per call.
- Reports are created exclusively. If HTML creation fails after JSON creation, the JSON is retained and the tool reports the partial result; retry using a fresh destination.
- No upload, traffic replay, header inspection, body analysis, automatic source lookup, or edits to the original HAR.

## Development and validation

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run smoke:host
npm pack --dry-run
```

48 tests passed on Node 24 and 26. They cover actual CLI subprocesses, controlled output and failure text, input limits, phases, original-file preservation, and real Cordis tool dispatch/filesystem/sandbox/Loader integration. `smoke:host` is a real service composition, not a CLI profile boot or a live-LLM test.

The packed bundle was separately installed through the actual CLI into fresh temporary Profiles on Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2`, then booted with `runProfile` and exercised through `har_triage`. Source bytes were unchanged; output omitted the synthetic canary; overwrite and workspace-escape attempts were refused. HMR was disabled only in those temporary Profiles. The alpha host emitted three unrelated Typert activation warnings; rc.2 did not. No LLM or real credentials were used.

Browser checks covered status filtering, signal-to-request navigation, correct source locators, no console errors, and a 390-pixel layout without page-level overflow. The demo and regression captures are synthetic; real-user usefulness is not yet validated.

## Related tools

[net-debug](https://github.com/JohnXu22786/net-debug) is an existing Harness HTTP client with history, replay and HAR export. [harlite](https://github.com/brucehart/harlite) already offers extensive HAR analysis, SQL, waterfall and HTML reporting. This plugin does not replace those tools: its narrower purpose is a Harness-native, no-external-binary, allowlisted evidence path for agent-assisted debugging.

MIT licensed.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: rewrite assistant replies in the persisted session log in place, so later turns read your version. DSH 插件：就地改写会话落盘记录里的助手回复，后续轮次读到的是改写后的版本。也支持伪造伪造回复，刷新就变回去，不影响流程。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-reply-forge-v2

DSH 桌面端插件 v2：**真伪造**——改写的 AI 回复进入会话落盘记录，被大模型
当作真实历史采信，且会话可继续对话。

与 v1（`dsh-reply-forge`，只做本机渲染层伪造）**完全独立**：独立仓库、
独立插件 id、独立安装链路。v1 封版不再演进；v2 不是 v1 的功能升级，
是另一条技术路线。

## 三大目标（验收标准）

1. **dsh 桌面端加载不会崩溃**——bundle 契约、注册 id、patch 插入全部
   合规；与 v1 可分别启用、互不踩踏；
2. **伪造回复会被大模型认同**——改写内容进入会话上下文，下一轮请求
   模型读到的就是伪造历史（含签名降级通道处理）；
3. **还能继续对话**——改写后会话完整性不破坏：可正常打开、可继续
   流式输出、投影/状态机不错位，且可回滚。

## 当前状态（2026-10-15）

**v2.0 与 v2.2 已实现；v2.2.1 修复了两处真机 bug（会话 id 寻址 + 记录缓存过期），
已安装进 desktop profile，等重启 DSH 生效。**
设计与实证见 [PLAN.md](PLAN.md)。

| 阶段 | 内容 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| v2.0 | 关闭态落盘改写器（CLI） | ✅ 实现完成，读取侧验收通过 |
| v2.0 | 真机重启后模型侧采信 | ✅ 用户实测通过（编辑内容被大模型认可） |
| v2.1 | 运行态写入（探针先行） | ⬜ 未开工 |
| v2.2 | UI 合一（dsh 插件形态） | ✅ 实现完成，已安装 |
| v2.2 | 真机重启后 UI 生效 | ✅ 用户实测可用（含两条回复的伪造） |
| v2.2.1 | 真机 bug 修复 | ✅ 已修（详见 PLAN §9.8），待重启验证 |

已落地的代码：

**写入内核（纯 ESM、零依赖）**

- `src/session-log.mjs` —— 只读层（多帧 zstd JSONL 解析、正文块收窄），
  从 v1 移植，自带多个真实会话的解析验证史；
- `src/session-write.mjs` —— 写入器核心：**seq+块索引 / 指纹**双寻址、
  `expectText` 陈旧校验、剥签名、多帧重组、原子写、写后自读校验；
- `src/checkout.mjs` —— 会话副本检出的公共逻辑。

**插件形态（v2.2）**

- `.dsh-plugin/index.mjs` —— host half：只声明 `inject: ['webServer']`，
  `apply()` 全程 try/catch，任何异常都不会拖垮宿主启动；
- `.dsh-plugin/server/routes.mjs` —— 两条 HTTP 路由：读块列表 / 执行写入。
  写路由带自定义头校验、参数校验、超长拒绝，业务失败一律 200 + `ok:false`；
- `.dsh-plugin/client/index.mjs` —— client half：在每条助手回复下挂操作条，
  就地编辑器双出口（`仅本机渲染` / `写入会话记录`）。会话 id 取自宿主渲染的
  `data-conversation-session` 属性——dsh 的 URL 里没有会话 id（见 PLAN §9.7）；
  记录比页面旧时自动重读补定位，不让用户对着一句过时的「对不上」干瞪眼（§9.8）；
- `.dsh-plugin/client/record.mjs` —— 磁盘记录访问层 + DOM↔磁盘两级匹配；
- `.dsh-plugin/client/{picker,markdown,classify,store,styles}.mjs` ——
  从 v1 移植的 UI 模块（前缀全部改为 `rf2-`，与 v1 严格隔离）；
- `.dsh-plugin/client.js` —— 构建产物（由 `scripts/build-client.mjs` 内联）。

**脚本**

- `scripts/forge-session.mjs` —— v2.0 写入 CLI（含 `--dry-run` / `--restore` /
  `--seq` / `--block-index` / dsh 运行中拒绝写入）；
- `scripts/install.mjs` / `enable.mjs` / `disable.mjs` / `profile-lib.mjs` ——
  安装 / 启用 / 关闭（**只改静态配置，绝不跑 pnpm**）；
- `scripts/build-client.mjs` —— client half 内联构建器（`--check` 校验新鲜度）；
- `scripts/host-oracle.mjs` —— 宿主预言机：用宿主自己的 dsh 起 slim host，
  直连 RPC 读回改写后的会话，双跑（伪造 vs 原始）有区分度；
- `scripts/provider-oracle.mjs` —— 照抄 App 真实启动配方起完整 desktop
  profile，读 provider 注册表（用于定位 13 渠道故障）；
- `scripts/session-anatomy.mjs` —— 会话解剖 / 上下文预算体检（只读），
  回答「这个会话还能不能继续对话」；
- `scripts/frame-anatomy.mjs` —— 帧结构解剖辅助工具。

测试 **73/73**：`session-log` 11 + `session-write` 15 + `session-anatomy` 7 +
`client` 23 + `routes` 15 + `build` 2。跑法：

```bash
for f in tests/*.test.mjs; do node "$f"; done
```

## 安装 / 启用 / 关闭

三个一键脚本（双击即可，不需要命令行）：

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `安装插件.bat` | 首次安装：建链接、写依赖、登记 lockfile、加入 bundles |
| `启用插件.bat` | 已装但被关掉时，加回 bundles（不需要重新安装） |
| `关闭插件.bat` | 停用：从 bundles 摘掉（保留链接与依赖，可秒开回来） |

三者都**只修改 dsh 启动时读取的静态配置**，不执行 pnpm。安装脚本默认会
顺手把 v1 从 bundles 里摘掉（两个插件同时启用会挂出两条操作条），但保留
v1 的依赖与链接，v1 用它自己的 `启用插件.bat` 就能开回来。想两个都开：
`node scripts/install.mjs --keep-v1`。

**改完必须完全退出并重启 DSH 才生效。**

## 与 v1 的关系

| | v1（dsh-reply-forge） | v2（本仓库） |
|---|---|---|
| 伪造层 | 浏览器渲染层（localStorage 覆盖） | 会话落盘记录（zstd JSONL） |
| 模型可见 | 否 | **是** |
| 落盘文件 | 一个字节都不碰 | 受控改写（带备份/回滚） |
| 适用 | 录屏/演示/截图 | 让模型采信伪造上下文 |

`src/session-log.mjs` 是从 v1 移植的只读层（多帧 zstd JSONL 解析、
assistant/message 文本块收窄），作为 v2 写入器的地基，自带多个真实
会话的解析验证史。

plugins.description: 面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Claude Code 风格终端界面，支持 Windows、macOS 与 Linux，兼容透明终端、VS Code 主题和自定义配色。
plugins.readme_text:
> **Release compatibility:** The current tested Host is official `0.2.0-rc.2`. SeekTTY `1.3.0` is paired with that Host. See the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md) for changes and installation, and the [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md) for exact package evidence.

SeekTTY

A terminal workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

Overview · Quick start · Clarify and Plan · Features · Compatibility

English · 中文

--- ## Overview Run `deepseek` from a project directory to use the native Agent, Session, model, permission, Settings, Profile, plugin, and persistence services of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in one terminal workspace. SeekTTY is the terminal surface; Harness remains the owner of runtime state. Models, Providers, Agent Presets, permissions, commands, tools, Settings, Skills, MCP servers, and marketplace sources are discovered from the running Harness. Capabilities added by upstream or third-party Bundles therefore appear without being hard-coded into SeekTTY. For requirements that still need definition, the optional [Clarify Host plugin](https://github.com/Hilbert-beinghappy/dsh-plugin-clarify) adds a guided `/clarify` workflow. It asks focused questions, updates a reviewable Draft after each answer, and returns the accepted Draft to the composer. Harness-native `/plan` can then turn the submitted requirement into an implementation plan. ## Development checkout Build and install a local SeekTTY package from the repository root: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm run build pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false ./seektty-1.3.0.tgz dsh --profile tui ``` Use the local tarball for source development and testing. For the released package, use the exact npm version below. ## Quick start Install the published SeekTTY release on its verified official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 dsh --profile tui ``` These commands install the prebuilt Bundle through native `dsh plugin` reconciliation. The per-command pnpm option avoids the pnpm 11 Global Virtual Store layout that the Cordis loader in the currently tested dsh releases cannot reliably load. SeekTTY never changes global pnpm configuration. Clarify and Auxiliary Runtime are optional, not default dependencies; their historical joint acceptance is listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-verification). The exact `seektty@1.3.0` npm package is documented in the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### Bare `deepseek` launcher After installing `dsh`, install the same SeekTTY release globally and pin Profile reconciliation to its exact npm version: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 export SEEKTTY_SPEC=seektty@1.3.0 deepseek ``` PowerShell uses the same exact npm spec: ```powershell pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false 'seektty@1.3.0' $env:SEEKTTY_SPEC='seektty@1.3.0' deepseek ``` `deepseek` requires `dsh` on `PATH`, or `DSH_BIN` pointing to its executable. Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: Keeps archived sessions out of the DSH conversation list and adds a panel to restore them or delete them permanently - session log, archive and pin records, and projection cache.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-archive-purge

Keeps archived sessions out of the DSH conversation list, and gives them one place to be restored — or **deleted for good**, which DSH itself deliberately has no path for.

> Looking for the npm name `dsh-archive-manager`? That one belongs to a different, unrelated
> plugin. This is `dsh-archive-purge`.

![The archived-session panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joyboy-yy/dsh-archive-purge/main/docs/panel.png)

*Every screenshot here is rendered from invented sessions — no real titles, paths or sizes.*

## The two gaps it closes

DSH can archive a session, but:

- **Archiving is only a view concern.** The sidebar keeps rendering archived rows whenever *View options → Archived* is set to show them, and it keeps them in archived search results too. There is no switch that means "never show these".
- **Nothing ever deletes a session.** `dsh-client-ui-workspace` documents no session deletion and `dsh-session-persistence` documents no delete seam, so archived sessions accumulate on disk forever.

This plugin closes both: it pins archived sessions out of the list, and it owns the erase path.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-archive-purge
```

Use your own profile name in place of `desktop` (for example `web`). Then switch it on under **Settings → Plugins**, where it appears as `dsh-archive-purge`. Turning it off disables the host routes and the browser panel together and leaves session data untouched.

## What it does

| | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Always hidden** | In the sidebar conversation list, an archived session row is never shown — whatever *View options → Archived* is set to. A component registered on `shell.overlay` writes `[data-row-key="session:<id>"]{display:none}` for every id in the registry's `archivedSessionIds`, plus a fallback rule keyed on the accessible description so archived search-result rows are covered as well. |
| **Filter reset** | The browser-persisted `dsh.workspace.view.v5` has its `archivedFilter` reset to the shipped default (`default`, i.e. "hide archived"), so the menu stops claiming "All conversations (show archived)" while showing nothing. |
| **Management panel** | A sidebar icon plus a centre-column panel lists every archived session with its workspace, path, disk footprint, creation time and child-session count; it supports search, multi-select and batch unarchive. |
| **Permanent delete** | Delete sessions one at a time or in bulk, behind a confirmation dialog that names the sessions, their size, and exactly what will be removed. |

The panel takes its colours from the host's `--dsw-alias-*` tokens and ships English and Chinese wording, so it follows whichever theme and locale the app is in rather than a look of its own.

## Permanent delete: the exact boundary

![The confirmation dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joyboy-yy/dsh-archive-purge/main/docs/confirm.png)

One delete removes four things:

1. **The session log directory** `<DSH_HOME>/sessions/<project>/<encoded-session-id>/` — the session's own directory, every format generation in it, and any session-local artifact;
2. **The projection-cache record** `<DSH_HOME>/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`;
3. **The archive and pin records** (`archivedSessionIds` / `pinnedSessionIds` in the workspace registry);
4. **The row in your browser** — announced through the session controller's own `api-session/removed` remote event (`@mode emit`) so the client drops the row instead of leaving a clickable ghost.

**Deliberately kept:** attachment files. Attachments are content-addressed and may be shared with other sessions, so they are out of scope. The panel says so at the bottom. An archived entry whose log is already gone from disk only has its record cleaned up, and the button reads "Clear record" instead.

## Refusals run before any write

![A batch that skipped one session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joyboy-yy/dsh-archive-purge/main/docs/refusals.png)

A batch reports each outcome separately: what was deleted and how much it freed, what had no log left to delete, and what was refused — named, with the reason.

- The session is **not in the archive set** → skipped. Deletion is only ever available for archived sessions.
- An **agent for that session still exists in this process** (`ctx.agents.get(id)`) → refused (`live`). An agent may already hold the log's write handle, and deleting the file underneath it would let the writer resurrect the log.
- The `workspace/session-activity` waterfall still reports **work in progress** → refused (`active`).
- The target directory is not **inside the configured sessions root**, or its name is not exactly the encoded session id → refused (`outside-root`).

Being merely *loaded* is deliberately **not** a refusal reason: the browser keeps an in-memory mirror for every rendered session row and never releases it, so refusing on that would make every archived session undeletable after enough browsing. The gate matches DSH's own archive gate (the activity waterfall) plus one cheaper agent check. Skipped and failed sessions are listed individually in the panel, with the reason.

## Ghost rows, and the two layers that remove them

DSH's browser session list is **event-driven**: it only adds and removes entries in response to `api-session/added` / `api-session/removed`. A deleted session also leaves the archive set, so in the sidebar it goes from "hidden" to "should be shown" — and the cached row becomes a visible, clickable row that fails with `session/not-found` when opened.

Two layers remove it:

- **Host side (authoritative).** After a successful delete and *before* the archive set is rewritten, the host emits `ctx.emit('api-session/removed', id)` — the remote event the session controller defines and forwards for exactly this fact. The client receives a `{ kind: 'remove', sessionId }` change and drops the row. Emitting before the registry write avoids a flash where the row is un-hidden and then disappears.
- **Client side (self-healing fallback).** The inventory carries `persistedIds` — the session ids the host's persistence layer actually knows. The panel diffs the browser's cached ids against it, folds the remainder into the same hide rule, and shows the count under the title. The diff is recomputed on every read rather than accumulated, so one failed read cannot permanently hide a live session. Ids deleted within this page session are tracked separately as a union, since that needs no read to take effect.

**If you deleted sessions before both layers existed**, those leftover rows need one page reload to disappear — the client re-fetches the list from the host on load. Deletions made afterwards do not leave them.

## Known leftovers

- **Dangling ids in workspace membership.** `tables.workspaces.<id>.sessionIds` is a persisted member array and the host exposes no "remove a member" operation (`insertSessionBefore` only inserts and orders). A deleted session's id therefore stays in that array. DSH tolerates missing members — it looks up a summary while deriving rows and skips what it cannot find — so this never renders as a row. It is bookkeeping residue, not a UI problem.
- **Agent lifetime.** Archiving only stops, hides and gates a session; it does not destroy the agent. Agents are reclaimed when the agent-loop provider unloads or the process exits. A session archived in the current DSH process is therefore refused by this plugin until you restart DSH. See *Refusals* above.

## Maintenance notes

- To land a delete precisely, the host half **copies verbatim** the `encodeSegment` function from `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`. If a DSH upgrade changes the session directory layout, that function has to follow it. Until then a delete refuses (because the directory name is not the encoded session id, or holds no session log) rather than removing the wrong thing.
- The client hide rule depends on the sidebar's `data-row-key="session:<id>"` attribute, which `dsh-client-ui-workspace` adds itself. If that ever changes, the `aria-description` fallback rule still applies.
- There is **no build step and no runtime dependency**: both halves are plain ESM shipp

plugins.description: Normify · DSH 插件：把项目架构写成归一化的分形模块树，三层校验（写时 / 校验 / 冻结回执）、30 个 normify_* 工具 + normify-gen 技能，一键渲染单文件交互式架构图；支持伴随式开发（change_open → brief → check → 实施 → refresh → change_close）。
plugins.readme_text:
English · 简体中文

Normify · 归一化框架图构建器

把整个项目描述成一棵"人机共读"的分形模块树：AI 负责分析与创作，确定性引擎负责校验、编译与渲染 —— 点开任意模块，就是一张更精细的子图。

--- ## 0. 一句话 Normify 是 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件**，也是**一套写给 AI 用的开发流程**： - **给 AI 的**：`normify-gen` 技能 + **31 个 `normify_*` 工具** —— 让模型把仓库分析成模块树结构数据， 并在后续开发中**先建图后编程、伴随编程改图**（计划态建树 → 逐个实现 → 关单收尾）。 - **给引擎的**：零容忍校验（L1 写时 / L2 全项目 / L3 冻结）+ 确定性编译（`tree.json` 等四件产物，SHA-256 冻结） + 渲染数据（`renders/`，决定"每一层怎么画"）。 - **给人的**：**单文件交互式架构图**（`normify.html`）—— 逐层下钻、悬停看介绍、一键中英切换、深链接、 多树、**API 直连箭头**、跨层聚合、缩放与搜索。零依赖，双击即开。 > 它不是"生成一张图就结束"的工具：结构数据与代码**互为契约**，每次改动都能被 `normify_sync` 检出漂移， > 并以 `normify_change_close`（**0 error 强制**）收尾，让"代码 → 架构图"永远同步。


引擎层：14 个模块、API 直连箭头（箭头锚定到具体 API 行）、带标签的子系统依赖、跨层聚合虚线

## 1. 它解决什么问题 | 痛点 | Normify 的做法 | | --- | --- | | 架构图一画完就过期 | 结构数据是**可校验的源数据**：`normify_sync` 按 `fingerprint` 检出漂移，`normify_change_close` 强制 0 error 收尾 | | 图太粗，看不出接口契约 | 粒度到**单一功能单元**，API 写在叶子上，箭头可锚定到具体 API（`from_api`/`to_api`） | | AI 改代码时"看不见全局" | `normify_brief` 给出目标模块契约、影响面（谁依赖我）、规则约束与验收清单 | | 设计先写代码后补文档，必然漂移 | **计划态先建树**（`state: planned`）→ 实现后 `normify_module_refresh(activate)` 自动转 active | | 结构规范靠人自觉 | `policy.yml` 架构规则（依赖方向 / 禁依赖 / 无环 / 深度 / 跨树 / 命名）由 `validate` 强制执行 | | 大仓库一次生成太重 | 增量再生成：只重建受影响子树，`layouts_to_review` 点名要复核的层 | ## 2. 核心特性 ### 2.1 数据模型：分形 + 零冗余 - **唯一元素**：整个数据库由无数个结构完全相同的**基本模块**构成（每个模块 = 一个 Markdown 文件）。 - **只存 `parent`**：单方向引用，`children` 由索引导出 —— 不会出现"父子各说各话"。 - **API 只在叶子存一次**：聚合、统计、索引全部是编译期派生数据（`tree.json` / `api-index.json`）。 - **两类边**：containment（树边，导航骨架）+ dependency（箭头，可跨子树、跨树，按 `kind` 着色）。 - **路径式 id + 不变 uid**：AI 沿 id 逐层定位（类二分查找）；`uid` 在改名/移动时保持不变，git diff 稳定。 - **深度不设上限**（0.5.0 起）：想有多细就拆多细，深度不再成为"合并模块"的理由。 ### 2.2 三层校验，fail-closed | 层 | 时机 | 内容 | | --- | --- | --- | | **L1** | 每次写入 | 必填字段、id 文法、uid、parent 一致性、双语长度、source/apis/deps 形状、state/replacement | | **L2** | `normify_validate` | 全项目：唯一性、文件↔id 映射、叶子/非叶子规则、API 键唯一、依赖目标、环、渲染数据交叉校验、架构规则、变更日志、（可选）仓库证据（source 存在性 + 指纹一致） | | **L3** | `normify_build` | 任何 error 都不产出产物；产出即 SHA-256 冻结进 `receipt.json` | 每条诊断都带 `severity / code / message / subject / evidence / supportedFixes` —— **AI 可自行修复**。 ### 2.3 渲染器：单文件、可下钻、API 直连 - 单文件 HTML（内联 CSS/JS，**零外部依赖**、零遥测），双击即开，可直接归档/发人。 - 逐层下钻 + 面包屑 + 搜索（模块名/API）+ 大纲视图 + API 浏览器。 - **API 直连**：叶子框内展示 API 明细行，箭头锚定到具体 API 行的端口；同一 API 行上的多条边自动扇形分离。 - 跨层依赖聚合为虚线 `×N`（默认隐藏，工具栏或 `?agg=1` 开启，悬停看明细）。 - 深链接：`#module=`、`#api=`、`#view=outline`、`?lang=zh|en`、`?agg=1`；缩放 / 悬停高亮 / 明暗主题。 - **几何自检**：仓库自带 `check-geometry.mjs`，逐层断言"线不出界 / 不贴框 / 不穿框 / 不压线"。 ### 2.4 伴随开发：先建图后编程 ``` change_open → brief → check → module_batch(state=planned) → 【写代码】 → module_refresh(activate) → change_close(0 error 强制) → verified + revision.after ``` - **计划态**：源码还不存在也能先建树（`fingerprint: pending`），`validate` 放行； - **禁止假激活**：源码没落地就 `activate` 直接被拒； - **收尾即闭环**：`change_close` 会刷新指纹 → 校验（0 error 强制）→ 编译（可选渲染）→ 标记 `verified`， 任何一步失败都不关闭，变更保持原状态； - **改图随代码**：`normify_sync` 用 `git diff` + 未跟踪文件定位受影响模块与指纹漂移，`module_patch` 跟随更新。 ### 2.5 架构规则先行（policy.yml） | 规则 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `dependency-direction` | 层顺序即允许的依赖方向（如 plugin → tools → engine），可控制同层是否允许 | | `forbid-dependency` | 禁止某些 from → to 的依赖（可按 kind / state 过滤） | | `acyclic` | 依赖图禁止成环（可含跨树） | | `max-depth` | id 段数上限（**可选**：不写就是不限，0.5.0 起默认不限） | | `cross-tree` | 跨树依赖策略：`forbid` / `allow` / `require-to-api` | | `naming` | 作用域内 id 段的命名正则 | 安装后 `normify_validate` / `normify_build` / `normify_check` 全部强制执行；**违规先改设计，不能绕过**。 ## 3. 最新变化 ### v0.5.4 · 把"第二轮 A/B 实测"暴露的 4 个工具缺陷修掉（当前版本） 第二轮 A/B 换了题目（**表格公式引擎 + CLI**，同一份规范、隐藏黑盒 88 项、外加**差分模糊测试**）。 两组最终 B 88/88、A 87/88（差异只有一条 §5.2 语义）；这一版修的是**工具侧**新暴露的 4 个坑： - **`mode:"patch"` 的静默 no-op 被拦下**：原来 `items:[{patch:{id, tags:[...]}}]`（少一层包装）会返回 `ok:true, count:1` 却**一个字段都没改**——最危险的"假成功"。现在直接报 `args/invalid-patch`， evidence 里给出收到的键与正确形状 `{patch:{id, patch:{...}}}`；单模块 `normify_module_patch` 传空补丁 同样报 `args/empty-patch`（只给 `expect_updated_at` 也不再静默通过）。 - **`normify_module_refresh` 不再强依赖 git**：`repoRoot` 不是 git 仓库时，以前直接 `refresh/git-failed` 失败（实测中 AI 只能 `git init` 才能激活模块）。现在改成**降级**：指纹照常重算、 `state` 照常激活，`revision` 保持模块原值，并给出 `refresh/git-unavailable` 警告与修法。 - **`change_open` 的 `acceptance` 报错具体化**：以前把 `{zh,en}` 写进 acceptance 只有一句笼统报错； 现在明确写出"**第 N 条不是非空字符串（收到 …）：验收标准只接受纯字符串**"，并提示双语描述写进 `title`/`intent`。 - **`normify_help` 支持 `topic:"tool:<工具名>"`**：`tools` 主题现在每个工具都带**必填/可选**摘要， 新主题可按需打印**完整参数树**（类型 / 描述 / 必填，由注册表实时生成、与运行时校验同源）。 实测里 AI 为确认 `mode=patch` 的嵌套形状去读了插件源码——这条主题正是为了消灭这种绕路。 ### v0.5.3 · 把「伴随编程实测」暴露的 4 个摩擦点修掉 这四个问题来自一次真实的 A/B 对照实验：两个 AI 用同一份规范写同一个后端，一个带插件走伴随流程、一个纯手写 （最终代码在隐藏黑盒验收上都是 **42/42**）。插件组多交付了 41 模块 / 110 API / 10 层的结构数据，但也踩到了下面 4 个坑： - **`normify_help` 支持 `topic`**：此前它完全忽略入参，只返回同一份字段速查 —— 实测里 AI 为了拿准 `change_open` / `layout_upsert` / `change_close` 的参数名，只能去读插件源码（多花约 4 分钟）。 现在按主题返回：`fields`（默认）/ `deps`（箭头与 API 直连）/ `renders` / `flow`（伴随流程）/ `tools`（工具清单）/ `policy` / `errors`（常见诊断码与修法）/ `all`；**传错主题会直接报错并列出可用主题**，不再静默忽略。 - **项目初始化通道**：新增第 31 个工具 `normify_project_init` —— 建 `normify-/` + 默认架构规则， 可选 `root` 一步创建"计划态根模块"（幂等）；同时 `normify_change_open` 现在也会**自动建项目目录** （此前报 `project/no-modules`，AI 只能用 `module_batch {items:[],dry_run:true}` 绕过去）； `normify_brief` 遇到不存在的模块会给出"先 init / 先建树 / 改用 task"的可执行提示。 - **批量诊断的因果链**：一条 `label-too-long` 曾连带出 3 条 `dep/target-missing`（因为 L1 失败的模块会被移出批次工作集）， AI 只能去读源码才能确认根因。现在连带错误改报 `dep/target-dropped` / `structure/parent-dropped`， 在 message 与 evidence 里点明**根因诊断码**，并在失败响应的 `root_causes` 里直接列出被丢弃的模块（附 `hint`）。 - **「API 直连」引导**：两端都声明了 API 却没写 `from_api` / `to_api` 的箭头，`normify_validate` 会给出**聚合** warning `dep/unanchored`（条数 + 前 3 条示例）。这正是实验里被浪费的能力：110 条 API 声明，54 条箭头 0 条锚定 —— 不锚定，箭头就只能落在框边，钉不到 API 行上。**引导≠放宽**：锚错键仍然是 error。 ### v0.5.2 · 修掉三处会写坏数据的真实缺陷 - **`normify_module_upsert` 的必填表不再丢失**：`parameters.required` 恢复为 `["frontmatter"]`， `frontmatter` 的 9 个必填字段（uid / id / parent / name / description / source / revision / updated_at / fingerprint） 也重新出现在 schema 里。此前嵌套 schema 被二次编译，必填表被整段丢掉 —— 模型看到的约束与运行时实际校验不一致。 - **`normify_module_move` 迁移渲染数据时重写内容**：`id` / `order` / `groups.children` / `edge_hints` 全部改写到新 id， 并同步维护**旧父级**（删掉已迁出子模块的引用）与**新父级**（把新 id 补进 `order`）。 修复前：move 完之后项目立刻被 L2 判为 `layout/id-mismatch` + `layout/order-child` 等（实测 8–9 个 error，0.5.2 后为 0）。 - **晋升为容器时不再把 API 留在容器上**：叶子被晋升（显式 `normify_module_promote`、写子模块自动晋升、move 到叶子底下） 时，容器上残留的 `apis` 会被摘除，并回报 `structure/api-dropped-on-promote` 警告（附丢失的 API 键清单）—— 修复前项目会直接卡在 `api/non-leaf`。 - **API 默认全展开**：渲染数据字段 `max_api_rows` 缺省 **0 = 全部展开**，叶子上的 API 一行不折叠；需要收窄时显式写 1..48。 -
